mainTopic: Leadership as service, the אשר/אשרי teachings, the 'one path' of צדיקים and פושעים, לוט's intent, and the value of acts done לשמה and שלא לשמה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story: a position of leadership is really a job of serving the people. Next, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי reads אשר in 'אשר נשיא יחטא' as אשרי: happy is the generation whose king admits even an accidental sin. When רבא בריה דרבה challenges this, the גמרא answers that only here the פסוק changed its usual wording. The same wordplay leads to two readings of a פסוק in קהלת about צדיקים and רשעים in this world, followed by a story where רבא blesses two students who learned and also became wealthy. Then רבי יוחנן, ריש לקיש and the גמרא search for the right example of 'one path' where צדיקים walk and פושעים stumble, and they settle on לוט and his daughters. A long discussion then proves that לוט meant to sin and was not helpless. More teachings about לוט and about intention follow: עולא compares תמר and זמרי, and רב נחמן בר יצחק teaches that an עבירה לשמה is equal to a מצוה שלא לשמה, using יעל as his proof. רב adds that one should do מצוות even שלא לשמה, proving it from בלק, whose offerings earned him רות as a descendant. The amud ends as רבי יוחנן begins to show that ה׳ rewards even modest speech, and that proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Leadership is servitude, not power
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of an earlier story: the leader tells the people he is appointing that he is giving them servitude, and he proves it from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: I am giving you servitude, as it says: 'And they spoke to him, saying: If today you will be a servant to this people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story that began before this section. The speaker tells the men he is appointing to office that a leadership position is really a job of serving the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the advice the elders gave רחבעם: a king who serves the people will keep their loyalty. So the point is that an appointment to public office is a duty to serve, not a gift of power.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: A leadership position in the community is a role of service, not a position of control.

phrases.english: I am giving you servitude,
phrases.notes: This finishes a story from just before this section. He is telling the men he appointed that their new job is to serve.

phrases.english: as it says: 'And they spoke to him, saying:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הַיּוֹם תִּהְיֶה עֶבֶד לָעָם הַזֶּה״.
phrases.english: If today you will be a servant to this people.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 12:7

steps.triggerLanguage: עַבְדוּת אֲנִי נוֹתֵן לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a story that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Public office means serving the people.

steps.title: Happy is the generation whose king brings an offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי reads אשר in 'אשר נשיא יחטא' as אשרי, meaning 'happy'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'When a king sins.' רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said: Happy is the generation whose king brings an offering for his accidental sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new teaching. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי says that a generation whose king brings a קרבן for an accidental sin is a fortunate generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אשר ('when') sounds like אשרי ('happy'). רבן יוחנן בן זכאי uses that sound to teach praise for a king who humbly admits even a mistake he made by accident (שוגג).

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the king, the top political ruler
An offering brought in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'When a king sins'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:22

phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said:
Happy is the generation whose king
phrases.notes: He is reading the word אשר ('when') as if it said אשרי ('happy').

phrases.english: brings an offering for his accidental sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״אֲשֶׁר נָשִׂיא יֶחֱטָא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, though it is still about how leaders should behave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word אשר in the פסוק about the king hints at אשרי: happy is the generation whose king atones for his accidental sin.

steps.title: Why that generation is happy: two קל וחומר arguments
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי explains his praise with two קל וחומר arguments: one about regular people and one about deliberate sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: If its king brings an offering, do you even need to say what a regular person will do? And if he brings an offering for an accidental sin, do you even need to say what he will do about a deliberate one?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי explains why such a generation is fortunate. A king who admits small mistakes sets a standard that carries over to everyone else and to more serious sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first קל וחומר: if even the proud king brings a קרבן, then surely a הדיוט (regular person) will too. The second: if the king atones for a sin he did by accident, then surely he will do תשובה for a sin he did on purpose (מזיד).

keyTerms.meaning: Do you even need to say? (it is obvious)

steps.whatToRemember: The praise is not that the king sinned. It is that he admits it, and his humility lifts the whole generation.
steps.confusionAlert: Bringing a קרבן for a deliberate sin is not what the second argument means. It means that a king this sincere will surely repent for his deliberate sins too.

phrases.english: If its king brings an offering,
do you even need to say what a regular person will do!
And if he brings an offering for his accidental sin,
do you even need to say what he will do about his deliberate sin!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם נָשִׂיא שֶׁלּוֹ מֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן, צָרִיךְ אַתָּה לוֹמַר מַהוּ הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the 'happy' דרשה in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king's humility over accidental sins proves that the people, and the king himself with his deliberate sins, will also seek atonement.

steps.title: Challenge: other verses also say אשר
steps.stepSummary: רבא בריה דרבה objects: if אשר means 'happy', then פסוקים about stealing from הקדש, and even about ירבעם בן נבט, would have to mean 'happy' too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא son of רבה challenged this: If so, then about the verse 'that which he sinned from the holy he shall pay', and about ירבעם בן נבט, of whom it says 'who sinned and caused others to sin', would you also say that the generation is happy?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בריה דרבה attacks the דרשה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. The word אשר shows up in many פסוקים about sinners where 'happy' makes no sense at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a common word like אשר always hinted at אשרי, we would get absurd readings. One example is a פסוק about a person who misused holy property. The worst example is ירבעם בן נבט, who led all of Israel into sin. So the challenge is: what makes אשר special in the פסוק about the king?

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it (raised a strong objection)
If that is so (leads into an absurd result)
The king who led Israel into idol worship

phrases.english: Rava son of Rabba challenged this:
If so, regarding what is written:
'And that which he sinned from the holy, he shall pay',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:16

phrases.english: and regarding Jeroboam son of Nevat, about whom it is written:
'who sinned and who caused others to sin',
phrases.notes: מלכים א 14:16

phrases.english: would you also say that the generation is happy?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the method behind the דרשה in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of אשר as אשרי in 'אשר נשיא יחטא'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: the same word appears about ירבעם and others, where 'happy' would be ridiculous.

steps.title: Answer: the verse changed its usual wording
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about the king is different, because the Torah departed from its normal wording only there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because the verse changed its wording.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא בריה דרבה's challenge. The word אשר alone is not the hint. The hint is that the Torah switched wording in this one spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the nearby פסוקים about the כהן גדול, the community and the individual, the Torah says אם ('if'). Only for the king does it switch to אשר. In the other פסוקים רבא brought, אשר is simply the normal word, so there is nothing to explain.
steps.whatToRemember: A דרשה from an ordinary word needs a reason, such as the פסוק breaking its own pattern.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic tool in reading the Torah: when a passage breaks its own pattern, the change itself is meant to teach something.

phrases.english: Here it is different,
because the verse changed its wording.
phrases.notes: The nearby פסוקים in ויקרא 4 all say אם ('if'). Only the king's פסוק says אשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָכָא, דְּשַׁנִּי קְרָא בְּדִבּוּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on a change in the פסוק's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner thought the דרשה rested only on the word אשר, which would apply everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: The דרשה rests on the Torah switching from אם to אשר only for the king, so other uses of אשר teach nothing.

steps.title: The righteous suffer here, the wicked prosper here
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא explains a פסוק in קהלת: happy are the צדיקים who get the treatment of the wicked in this world, and woe to the רשעים who get the reward of the righteous in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא taught: What is the meaning of the verse 'There is a vanity that is done on the earth, etc.'? Happy are the righteous, who receive in this world what the wicked receive in the World to Come. Woe to the wicked, who receive in this world what the righteous receive in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching that plays on the same word, אשר / אשרי. It explains why good people sometimes suffer and bad people sometimes do well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in קהלת repeats the word אשר, and רב נחמן reads it as אשרי, just like the previous דרשה. A צדיק who suffers in עולם הזה is fortunate, because he settles his account here and is spared later. A רשע who prospers in עולם הזה is in trouble, because he uses up his reward here.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained a פסוק in a deeper, homiletic way

steps.whatToRemember: What looks unfair in עולם הזה is balanced in עולם הבא: the צדיקים pay here and are rewarded later.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'like the deeds of the wicked of the World to Come' does not mean the צדיקים act like רשעים. It means they get, in this world, the suffering that רשעים get in עולם הבא.

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda taught:
What is the meaning of what is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״יֶשׁ הֶבֶל אֲשֶׁר נַעֲשָׂה עַל הָאָרֶץ וְגוֹ׳״ –
phrases.english: 'There is a vanity that is done on the earth, etc.'
phrases.notes: קהלת 8:14. The rest of the פסוק talks about good people treated like bad people, and bad people treated like good people.

phrases.english: Happy are the righteous,
to whom comes what happens to the wicked
in the World to Come, already in this world.
Woe to the wicked,
to whom comes what happens to the righteous
in the World to Come, already in this world.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the same אשר / אשרי wordplay from steps 2 to 5 and applies it to a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדיקים who suffer in עולם הזה are fortunate, and רשעים who prosper in עולם הזה are unfortunate, because the reckoning is settled in reverse in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבא asks why צדיקים should have to suffer
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to רב נחמן בר רב חסדא's idea that צדיקים are 'happy' when they suffer in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is that to say that if the righteous enjoy both worlds, it would be bad for them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the explanation from Step 6. That explanation said צדיקים are lucky when they suffer in this world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא made suffering in this world sound like a good thing for צדיקים. רבא asks why that should be. If a צדיק gets reward in this world and in עולם הבא, there is nothing wrong with that.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a question that shows an idea doesn't make sense)
two worlds: this world and the World to Come

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ צַדִּיקֵי אִי אָכְלִי תְּרֵי עָלְמֵי
phrases.english: Is that to say that if the righteous enjoy two worlds
phrases.notes: Literally 'eat two worlds.' He means getting good things in this world and also in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: would it be bad for them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ צַדִּיקֵי אִי אָכְלִי תְּרֵי עָלְמֵי מִי סְנֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק in קהלת given in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא's claim that צדיקים are 'happy' when they suffer in this world.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no reason to call suffering good for a צדיק. Enjoying both worlds would not hurt him.

steps.title: רבא's own reading of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבא flips the reading: happy are the צדיקים who enjoy this world, and woe to the רשעים who suffer in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Happy are the righteous who receive in this world what the wicked usually get in this world. Woe to the wicked who receive in this world what the righteous usually get in this world.
steps.whatsHappening: Since he rejected the earlier reading, רבא now gives his own explanation of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this world, the רשעים often have an easy life and the צדיקים often suffer. רבא says a צדיק is lucky if he gets the easy life too. A רשע is in trouble if he gets the suffering that usually comes to צדיקים.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (brings in a new explanation in place of the old one)
like what happens to (here: the life experience of)

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Happy are the righteous
to whom it happens like the experience of the wicked
phrases.notes: In this world the wicked often have a comfortable life. רבא means the צדיקים get that comfort too.

phrases.english: of this world, in this world.
Woe to the wicked
to whom it happens like the experience of the righteous
of this world, in this world.

steps.confusionAlert: The words are the same as in Step 6, but the meaning is reversed. Here 'happy' means the צדיק enjoys this world. It does not mean he suffers in it.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading that רבא rejected in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדיקים are fortunate when they also enjoy this world. רשעים are unfortunate when they suffer in this world.

steps.title: רבא blesses two students who learned and became wealthy
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא tell רבא they finished tractates and bought land. רבא applies his reading of the פסוק to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב הונא son of רב יהושע came before רבא. He asked: Have you mastered this tractate and that tractate? They said yes. Have you become a little wealthy? They said yes, we bought a small piece of land. He said about them: Happy are the righteous who receive what the wicked of this world get, in this world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story showing רבא using his own reading in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two students were learned in Torah, so they count as צדיקים. They also became a bit wealthy, which is the kind of comfort the wicked usually enjoy. This fits רבא's reading exactly: a צדיק who also does well in this world is 'happy.'

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
came before Rava.
He said to them:
Have you mastered such-and-such tractate and such-and-such tractate?
They said to him: Yes.
Have you become a little wealthy?
They said to him: Yes,
for we bought a small piece of land.
He recited about them:
Happy are the righteous
to whom it happens like the experience of the wicked
who are in this world, in this world.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, a צדיק who also has a good life in this world is not losing anything. He is 'happy' twice over.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבא applying the reading he gave in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תלמידי חכמים who also become a bit wealthy fit רבא's 'happy are the צדיקים.'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's משל of two people eating the פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the פסוק in הושע with a משל: two people eat the קרבן פסח, one for the מצוה and one just to stuff himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What does the פסוק mean, 'For the ways of ה׳ are straight; the righteous walk in them, and sinners stumble in them'? It is like two people who roasted their פסח offerings. One ate it for the מצוה, and one ate it just to stuff himself. The one who ate it for the מצוה is 'the righteous walk in them.' The one who ate it to stuff himself is 'sinners stumble in them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רבי יוחנן explains a פסוק that seems to say the same path can lead one person up and another person down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says both the righteous and the sinners are 'in them,' meaning the same ways. רבי יוחנן says this means the same act: both people ate the very same פסח. The difference is only their intention. One did it for the מצוה, and the other did it for his appetite.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the meaning of what is written?
for the sake of the מצוה
gluttonous eating, overeating just to fill up

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"For the ways of ה׳ are straight,
and the righteous walk in them,
and sinners stumble in them"?
phrases.notes: הושע 14:10

phrases.english: It is like two people
who roasted their Pesach offerings.
One ate it for the sake of the מצוה,
and one ate it as gluttonous eating.
This one, who ate it for the sake of the מצוה:
"the righteous walk in them."
This one, who ate it as gluttonous eating:
"and sinners stumble in them."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching. It is connected by theme, since it also talks about צדיקים and רשעים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same act of eating the פסח counts as 'walking' when it is done for the מצוה and as 'stumbling' when it is done for gluttony.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the overeater still did the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש objects that a person who ate the פסח, even greedily, cannot be called a sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: You call him wicked? Granted, he did not do the מצוה in the best way, but didn't he eat the פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן's משל from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the second person a פושע, a real sinner. But the overeater still ate the קרבן פסח and fulfilled the מצוה. He only did it in a less-than-ideal way. That is not enough to call him a sinner who 'stumbles.'

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' here is רבה בר בר חנה, who was reporting רבי יוחנן's teaching.

phrases.english: You call him wicked?

phrases.aramaic: נְהִי דְּלָא עָבֵיד מִצְוָה מִן הַמּוּבְחָר,
phrases.english: Granted, he did not do the מצוה in the best way,
but didn't he eat the Pesach?

steps.triggerLanguage: רָשָׁע קָרֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משל in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the gluttonous eater of the פסח fits 'sinners stumble in them.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He still fulfilled the מצוה, even if not in the best way. Someone who does a מצוה cannot be called a פושע.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's משל of the wife and the sister
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives a new משל. Two men each do the same act. For one it is permitted, with his wife, and for the other it is a severe sin, with his sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like two people. This one has his wife and his sister with him in the house, and that one has his wife and his sister with him in the house. To one, his wife came. To the other, his sister came. The one whose wife came is 'the righteous walk in them.' The one whose sister came is 'sinners stumble in them.'
steps.whatsHappening: After his objection, ריש לקיש offers his own משל to explain the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משל, both men do the exact same physical act, so the פסוק's 'in them' still fits. But one act is fully permitted, while the other is a true עבירה, an ערוה. So the second man really is a פושע, which solves ריש לקיש's own question.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like two people:
this one has his wife and his sister with him in the house,
and that one has his wife and his sister with him in the house.
To one, his wife happened to come,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is speaking delicately here. It means each man was intimate with the woman who happened to come to him.

phrases.english: and to the other, his sister happened to come.
This one, to whom his wife came:
"the righteous walk in them."
And this one, to whom his sister came:
"and sinners stumble in them."

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש fixes his own problem: in his משל the second man commits a real עבירה, so he truly deserves the name פושע. Watch the next step, though: the גמרא rejects this משל because it has two different acts, not one path.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מָשָׁל לִשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי יוחנן's משל after ריש לקיש's objection in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק describes the same act that is permitted for one person and a real sin for another. That makes the second person a true פושע.

steps.title: The wife-and-sister example does not fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects ריש לקיש's משל. The פסוק speaks of one path, but his example has two different paths.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these comparable? We are talking about one path, and here there are two paths!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on ריש לקיש's משל. It says his example does not match the פסוק in הושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the צדיקים and the פושעים walk on the same ways. In ריש לקיש's case, one man is with his wife and the other is with his sister. Those are really two different acts, so it is not 'one path.'

keyTerms.meaning: Are these comparable? A phrase used to reject a comparison
One path, meaning the same action
Two paths, meaning two different actions

phrases.english: Are these comparable?
We are speaking of one path,
and here there are two paths!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? אֲנַן קָאָמְרִינַן חֲדָא דֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the משל ריש לקיש offered in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: ריש לקיש's משל of the wife and the sister
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק speaks of one path, meaning one and the same action shared by both people. His example has two different actions, one with a wife and one with a sister.

steps.title: The better example: לוט and his daughters
steps.stepSummary: The same act was done by לוט and by his daughters. They meant it for a מצוה and he meant it for an עבירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like לוט and his two daughters. The daughters, who meant it for the sake of a מצוה, fit 'the righteous will walk in them.' לוט, who meant it for the sake of an עבירה, fits 'and transgressors will stumble in them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new משל that really is 'one path.' One single act was done by both sides, but with opposite intentions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the action is literally the same act between the same people. The only difference is intention. The daughters intended a מצוה and לוט intended an עבירה. This fits the פסוק exactly: one path, and some walk in it while others stumble.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable or example used to explain something
For the sake of a מצוה, with a good intention
For the sake of a sin, with a bad intention

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the גמרא's final picture of the פסוק: the same act can be righteous or sinful depending on a person's intention.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like Lot and his two daughters.
They, who intended it for the sake of a מצוה:
"The righteous will walk in them."
phrases.notes: הושע 14:10

phrases.english: He, who intended it for the sake of a transgression:
"And transgressors will stumble in them."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מָשָׁל לְלוֹט וּשְׁתֵּי בְנוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected משל with one that truly has one path.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק in הושע fits לוט and his daughters: one act, with good intention on their side and sinful intention on his.

steps.title: Maybe לוט also meant well?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: how do we know לוט meant it for an עבירה? Perhaps he too intended a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he too intended it for the sake of a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the new משל. It asks how we know that לוט's intention was bad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole משל depends on לוט's intention being different from his daughters'. If he also meant it for a מצוה, then nobody 'stumbles' and the example fails.

phrases.english: But perhaps he too, for the sake of a מצוה,
intended it!
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'he intended.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא הוּא נָמֵי לְשֵׁם מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption in step 14 that לוט intended an עבירה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that לוט acted לשם עבירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the story proves his intention was bad, so maybe he meant well like his daughters.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the whole פסוק about לוט speaks of sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that the entire פסוק describing לוט's choice of the Jordan plain is said in the context of עבירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This entire פסוק is said in the sense of עבירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that לוט's character was already shown to be drawn to immorality. Its source is a פסוק earlier in his story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If לוט was already described as someone chasing desire, it makes sense that his intention with his daughters was bad too. The next step shows how each word of that פסוק hints at this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַפָּסוּק הַזֶּה לְשֵׁם עֲבֵירָה נֶאֱמַר.
phrases.english: This entire verse was said in the sense of transgression.
phrases.notes: The פסוק is בראשית 13:10, where לוט looks out and picks the well-watered Jordan plain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, כׇּל הַפָּסוּק הַזֶּה לְשֵׁם עֲבֵירָה נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוט might have intended a מצוה like his daughters.
steps.terutzMaskana: לוט's own פסוק shows him as drawn to sin, so his intention was לשם עבירה.

steps.title: Each word in לוט's פסוק hints at immorality
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן links each phrase of בראשית 13:10 to another פסוק about immorality or desire.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And לוט lifted' is like 'his master's wife lifted her eyes.' 'His eyes' is like שמשון saying 'take her for me, for she is pleasing in my eyes.' 'And he saw' is like 'שכם son of חמור saw her.' 'The whole plain of the Jordan' is like 'for a harlot, down to a loaf of bread.' 'That it was all well watered' is like 'I will go after my lovers who give me my bread, water, wool, flax, oil and drink.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן proves his claim word by word. He matches each phrase about לוט with the same word used in a פסוק about forbidden desire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting eyes recalls the wife of פוטיפר with יוסף. 'His eyes' recalls שמשון. 'Saw' recalls שכם. כיכר recalls the harlot's loaf. משקה recalls the unfaithful woman's 'drink' in הושע. Together they paint לוט as a man led by his desires.

keyTerms.meaning: A plain, and also a loaf of bread
Well watered, from the word for drink

phrases.english: "And Lot lifted up":
like "His master's wife lifted up her eyes."
phrases.notes: בראשית 39:7, about the wife of פוטיפר and יוסף.

phrases.english: "His eyes":
like "And Samson said, [etc.]

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתָהּ קַח לִי כִּי הִיא יָשְׁרָה בְעֵינָי״
phrases.english: get her for me, for she is pleasing in my eyes."
"And he saw":
like "And Shechem son of Hamor saw her."
"The whole plain of the Jordan":

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי בְעַד אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה עַד כִּכַּר לָחֶם״
phrases.english: like "For on account of a harlot, a man comes down to a loaf of bread."
phrases.notes: The link is the word כיכר, which means 'plain' about לוט and 'loaf' here.

phrases.english: "That it was all well watered":
like "I will go after my lovers, who give my bread and my water,
my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink."
phrases.notes: הושע 2:7. The words משקה and שקויי come from the same root, 'drink.'

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַיִּשָּׂא לוֹט״ – ״וַתִּשָּׂא אֵשֶׁת אֲדֹנָיו אֶת עֵינֶיהָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out רבי יוחנן's claim from step 16 phrase by phrase.
steps.raayaObject: That לוט's פסוק describes a man drawn to sin
steps.raayaSupportSource: Matching words in פסוקים about פוטיפר's wife, שמשון, שכם, the harlot in משלי, and the unfaithful woman in הושע

steps.title: But לוט was helpless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: לוט was drunk, so how can he be blamed for intending an עבירה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he was forced by circumstances beyond his control!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. לוט was drunk and did not know what was happening, so it seems he had no intention at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who is אנוס, forced or unaware, is not blamed. If לוט was fully unaware, he could not have intended an עבירה. That would break the משל of the two intentions.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, an opening word for a challenge
He was totally forced or helpless

phrases.english: But he was forced by circumstances beyond his control!
phrases.notes: He means לוט was drunk, and the פסוק says he did not know what happened.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מֵינָס אֲנִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion that לוט acted לשם עבירה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Blaming לוט for an intention to sin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone drunk and unaware is אנוס and has no intention, good or bad.

steps.title: The dot shows לוט knew when she got up
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי יוסי בר רבי חוני learns from the dot over the ו in בקומה that לוט knew when the older daughter got up.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי יוסי בר רבי חוני: Why is there a dot over the ו in 'when she arose' about the older daughter? To tell you that when she lay down he did not know, but when she got up he did know.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that לוט was not completely unaware. A dot in the תורה's text shows he realized what happened by the end of the first night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says he did not know 'when she lay down, nor when she arose.' The dot over בקומה weakens that word. It teaches that at her rising he did know. So לוט was aware of what had happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Dotted, with a dot written above a letter

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי חוֹנִי
phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Honi:
Why is there a dot over the vav
in "when she arose" of the older daughter?
phrases.notes: בראשית 19:33. In the תורה scroll a dot is written above this ו.

phrases.english: To tell you
that when she lay down he did not know,
but when she arose he knew.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי חוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual proof from a dot over a letter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוט was totally unaware and therefore אנוס.
steps.terutzMaskana: He knew when the older daughter got up, so he was not fully unaware.

steps.title: But what could לוט have done?
steps.stepSummary: Even if he knew afterward, the act was already done. What could he have done about it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what should he have done? What happened, happened!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Knowing after the fact does not help, because the first night was already over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His realizing it only when she got up means the act was finished. There seems to be nothing he could have changed, so he still looks blameless.

phrases.english: And what should he have done?
What happened, happened!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֶעְבַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the knowledge shown in step 19 makes him guilty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from the dot that לוט is to blame
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Knowing only after the act cannot make him responsible for an act already finished.

steps.title: He should not have drunk the next night
steps.stepSummary: Since he knew what happened, he should have learned not to drink again the next night. By drinking again he showed bad intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lesson from it: on the next night he should not have drunk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. לוט's guilt is not about the first night but about drinking again on the second night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he knew what had happened, he was warned. Choosing to get drunk again the next night means he let it happen with the younger daughter. That is why he counts as one who intended an עבירה.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical result or lesson from it

steps.whatToRemember: The same act was one path for both sides. לוט's daughters meant it for a מצוה and fit 'צדיקים ילכו בם.' לוט was drawn to desire and drank again knowingly, so he fits 'ופושעים יכשלו בם.'

phrases.english: The lesson from it is

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְפַנְיָא אַחֲרִינָא לָא אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְמִישְׁתֵּי.
phrases.english: that on the next night he should not have drunk.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ דִּלְפַנְיָא אַחֲרִינָא לָא אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְמִישְׁתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 by moving the blame to the second night.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifts the blame to a later, avoidable action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the first night was already over, לוט could not have done anything.
steps.terutzMaskana: Knowing what happened, he should have avoided drinking the next night. Drinking again shows intent to sin.

steps.title: רבה reads a פסוק in משלי as describing לוט
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains משלי 18:19 as describing לוט, who split from אברהם and caused permanent conflict between ישראל and עמון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה taught: What does the פסוק mean, 'A brother betrayed a strong city, and contentions are like the bars of a castle'? 'A brother betrayed a strong city' is לוט, who left אברהם. 'Contentions like the bars of a castle' means he caused conflict between ישראל and עמון, as it says: 'An עמוני and מואבי shall not enter the congregation of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the topic of לוט, רבה explains a פסוק in משלי as being about him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'brother' is לוט, אברהם's nephew, who walked away from him. The 'contentions' are the lasting separation between ישראל and עמון, his descendants. That separation shows up in the הלכה that an עמוני may not marry into ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded, explained a פסוק in a deeper way
What is the meaning of what is written
Men from the nations of עמון and מואב, descendants of לוט

phrases.english: Rabba expounded: what is the meaning of that which is written:
"A brother betrayed a strong city,
and contentions are like the bars of a castle"?
phrases.notes: משלי 18:19

phrases.english: "A brother betrayed a strong city":
this is Lot, who parted from Avraham.
"And contentions are like the bars of a castle":
that he cast contention between Israel and Ammon,
as it is stated: "An Ammonite and a Moabite shall not enter
into the congregation of the Lord."
phrases.notes: דברים 23:4

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבָּה, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that לוט has been shown to have bad intent, the גמרא brings more teachings that criticize him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משלי 18:19 refers to לוט, who left אברהם and caused permanent separation between ישראל and עמון.

steps.title: לוט separated for desire and his shame is taught everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רבי יצחק) reads משלי 18:1 as describing לוט: he separated from אברהם to chase desire, and his shame is revealed wherever Torah is taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught (some say it was רבי יצחק): What does the פסוק mean, 'One who separates seeks his desire; in all wisdom he is exposed'? 'One who separates seeks his desire' is לוט, who separated from אברהם. 'In all wisdom he is exposed' means his shame is revealed in בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות, as we learned in a משנה: an עמוני and מואבי are forbidden forever.
steps.whatsHappening: A second teacher reads another פסוק in משלי as being about לוט. This time the stress is on his desire and his public shame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק says לוט left אברהם to chase his desires. The word יִתְגַּלָּע sounds like נִתְגַּלָּה, 'revealed.' So every time people learn the משנה that עמוני ומואבי are forbidden forever, they are reminded where these nations came from.

phrases.english: Rava expounded, and some say it was Rabbi Yitzchak:
what is the meaning of that which is written:
"He who separates himself seeks desire;
in all sound wisdom he is exposed"?
phrases.notes: משלי 18:1. Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: "He who separates himself seeks desire":
this is Lot, who separated from Avraham.
"In all sound wisdom he is exposed":
that his shame was revealed
phrases.notes: יִתְגַּלָּע in the פסוק is read like נִתְגַּלָּה, 'was revealed.'

phrases.english: in synagogues and in study halls.
As we learned in a mishnah:
An Ammonite and a Moabite are forbidden with a permanent prohibition.
phrases.notes: Forbidden to marry into the Jewish people. This is the line everyone learns, and it keeps reminding them of לוט.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching. Like step 22, it reads a פסוק in משלי as being about לוט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוט left אברהם for desire, and his shame is publicized whenever the הלכה of עמוני ומואבי is learned.

steps.title: תמר and זמרי: the same kind of act with opposite results
steps.stepSummary: עולא compares תמר and זמרי. Both did an act of immorality, but תמר's led to kings and prophets, while זמרי's led to thousands of deaths.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: תמר acted immorally and זמרי acted immorally. From תמר came kings and prophets. Because of זמרי, tens of thousands of ישראל died.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching that matches the theme of the סוגיא: the intention behind an act matters. עולא sets two similar acts side by side. This prepares the ground for the next step's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the outside, תמר's act with יהודה and זמרי's act with כזבי look alike. The results were completely opposite. That shows the purpose behind an act can change what it really is.

phrases.english: And Ulla said:
Tamar acted immorally, and Zimri acted immorally.
phrases.notes: תמר was with יהודה in בראשית 38. זמרי was with כזבי in במדבר 25.

phrases.english: Tamar acted immorally:
kings and prophets came out of her.
Zimri acted immorally:
many tens of thousands of Israel fell.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר עוּלָּא: תָּמָר זִנְּתָה וְזִימְרִי זִינָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from לוט's bad intent to a general comparison of good and bad intent in similar acts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two similar acts of immorality had opposite results: blessing from תמר, disaster from זמרי.

steps.title: A sin for Heaven's sake is greater than a מצוה done for the wrong reason
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק teaches that an עבירה לשמה is greater than a מצוה שלא לשמה. His proof is that יעל is blessed more than the אמהות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: A sin done for the sake of Heaven is greater than a מצוה not done for its own sake, as it says: 'Blessed above women is יעל, wife of חבר the קיני; above women in the tent she will be blessed.' Who are the 'women in the tent'? שרה, רבקה, רחל and לאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק turns the idea into a rule and brings a פסוק to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק blesses יעל even more than the 'women in the tent,' which the גמרא identifies as the four אמהות. The גמרא understands יעל's act with סיסרא as an עבירה done for the sake of Heaven. Since she is ranked above the אמהות, it concludes that such a sin is greater than a מצוה done שלא לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin done for the sake of Heaven, with a holy purpose
A מצוה done for the wrong reason, not purely for Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: This is not yet the final version of the rule. In the next two steps the גמרא challenges the word 'greater' and changes it.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Greater is a transgression done for its sake
phrases.notes: 'For its sake' here means for the sake of Heaven, with a holy goal.

phrases.english: than a מצוה done not for its sake,
as it is stated: "Blessed above women shall be Yael,
the wife of Chever the Kenite;
above women in the tent shall she be blessed."
phrases.notes: שופטים 5:24

phrases.english: Who are the "women in the tent"?
Sarah, Rivkah, Rachel, and Leah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: גְּדוֹלָה עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ מִמִּצְוָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on עולא's comparison and states it as a general rule with a proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבירה לשמה is greater than a מצוה שלא לשמה, as shown by יעל being blessed above the אמהות.

steps.title: But רב says to do מצוות even for the wrong reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק using רב's teaching that a person should always do Torah and מצוות even שלא לשמה, because that leads to doing them לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person should always be involved in Torah and מצוות even not for their own sake, because by doing them not for their sake, he will come to do them for their sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the word 'greater.' רב treats a מצוה שלא לשמה as a good thing, so how can a sin be better than it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says a מצוה שלא לשמה is valuable, since it is the path to serving ה׳ purely. If so, it should not be ranked below a sin. That contradicts רב נחמן בר יצחק's statement that an עבירה לשמה is greater.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב's teaching, that one should do מצוות even שלא לשמה because it leads to לשמה, is a famous and widely quoted principle.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rav Yehudah say in the name of Rav:
A person should always engage in Torah and מצוות
even not for their own sake,
because from doing it not for its sake, he comes to do it for its sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule stated in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that an עבירה לשמה is 'greater than' a מצוה שלא לשמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב values a מצוה שלא לשמה as a positive step toward לשמה, so it cannot be ranked below a sin.

steps.title: Change 'greater than' to 'equal to'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: an עבירה לשמה is like, meaning equal to, a מצוה שלא לשמה, not greater than it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: a sin for the sake of Heaven is as great as a מצוה done not for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing one word in רב נחמן בר יצחק's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of מִמִּצְוָה ('than a מצוה'), read כְּמִצְוָה ('like a מצוה'). Now the two are equal, so a מצוה שלא לשמה keeps the positive value רב gave it. An עבירה לשמה still turns out to be something good.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (the גמרא changes the wording)
Like a מצוה, equal to a מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: Final version: an עבירה לשמה is equal to a מצוה שלא לשמה. Both have real value, and a מצוה שלא לשמה is still worth doing because it leads to לשמה.

phrases.english: Say instead: like a מצוה done not for its sake.
phrases.notes: Just one letter changes: מִ ('than') becomes כְּ ('like'). So 'greater than' becomes 'as great as.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: כְּמִצְוָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 26 by changing the wording of step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An עבירה לשמה is greater than a מצוה שלא לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: An עבירה לשמה is equal to a מצוה שלא לשמה, so רב's teaching stands.

steps.title: סיסרא's seven acts with יעל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק in שופטים to show that סיסרא was with יעל seven times at that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: That wicked man had relations seven times at that time, as the פסוק says: "Between her legs he crouched, he fell, he lay," and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the topic of יעל from the last steps, רבי יוחנן adds a detail about what happened between her and סיסרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the verbs 'crouched', 'fell' and 'lay' seven times in all, and רבי יוחנן reads each one as a separate act. This shows how far יעל went in her עבירה לשמה to save the Jewish people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
Seven acts of relations he performed,
that wicked man, at that time,
phrases.notes: 'That wicked man' is סיסרא, and 'at that time' means when he was in יעל's tent.

phrases.english: as it is stated:
"Between her legs he crouched, he fell, he lay, etc."
phrases.notes: שופטים 5:27. If you count the verbs in the whole פסוק, you get seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁבַע בְּעִילוֹת בָּעַל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail about יעל, whose עבירה לשמה was the topic of steps 25-27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סיסרא had relations with יעל seven times, learned from the seven verbs in שופטים 5:27.

steps.title: Didn't יעל enjoy the sin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if this happened seven times, surely יעל got some pleasure from the sin. So how can she be praised?
steps.simpleTranslation: But surely she was getting pleasure from the sin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that יעל acted purely לשמה, pointing out that she may have enjoyed the act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבירה לשמה is only praiseworthy if the person's whole intent is for Heaven. If יעל enjoyed the sin, her act would not be purely לשמה, and the praise she gets in step 25 would be hard to understand.

phrases.english: But surely she was getting pleasure
from a sin?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָא מִיתְהַנְיָא מֵעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the purity of יעל's intent, given the seven acts described in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יעל's act was an עבירה לשמה worthy of blessing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pleasure from the sin would mean she was not acting purely for Heaven, so she should not be praised.

steps.title: The 'good' of the wicked is bad to the righteous
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי teaches that anything 'good' coming from the wicked feels bad to the righteous, so יעל had no pleasure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: Even the good of the wicked is bad to the righteous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: a צדיק like יעל gets no enjoyment from anything that comes from a רשע like סיסרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that pleasure would come automatically. This answer says that for the righteous, what comes from the wicked is unpleasant. So יעל's act stayed fully לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: The good or favor of the wicked

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
Even the good of the wicked
is bad to the righteous.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ טוֹבָתָם שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים רָעָה הִיא אֵצֶל צַדִּיקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the assumption that she enjoyed it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יעל must have enjoyed the act, so it was not purely לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A צדיק finds the 'good' of a רשע unpleasant, so יעל felt no pleasure and acted fully for Heaven.
steps.whatToRemember: יעל's act counts as a true עבירה לשמה because she got no pleasure from it: the 'good' of the wicked is bad to the righteous.

steps.title: רב's rule and the proof from בלק's offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב's rule that one should learn and do מצוות even שלא לשמה is quoted again, now with a proof: בלק's 42 offerings earned him רות as a descendant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says in the name of רב: A person should always be involved in תורה and מצוות even שלא לשמה, because from שלא לשמה he comes to לשמה. For as a reward for the 42 offerings that בלק the wicked brought, he merited that רות came from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב's rule again, the one used in step 26 to challenge רב נחמן בר יצחק, and now adds the proof from בלק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלק brought his offerings only so he could curse ישראל, which is about as שלא לשמה as it gets. Still, he was rewarded with a great descendant, רות. This shows that even a מצוה done for the wrong reasons has real value.

keyTerms.meaning: A person should always be involved
Not for its own sake, for an outside motive
For its own sake, for Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion. It is the same רב quoted in step 26. The גמרא repeats it here so it can give the proof from בלק.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
A person should always be involved
in Torah and מצוות
even not for its own sake,
because from doing it not for its own sake, he comes to do it for its own sake,
for as a reward for forty-two offerings
phrases.notes: Look at במדבר 23: seven altars with a bull and a ram on each, brought three times, which adds up to 42.

phrases.english: that Balak the wicked offered,
he merited, and Ruth came out from him,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲסוֹק אָדָם בַּתּוֹרָה וּבַמִּצְוֹת אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב's rule from step 26 and gives the source behind it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should do תורה and מצוות even שלא לשמה, as בלק's self-serving offerings were still rewarded with רות as a descendant.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source in חז"ל for the value of a מצוה done שלא לשמה. It explains why step 27 would not let an עבירה לשמה be called 'greater' than it.

steps.title: רות descends from בלק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא gives the family line that links רות to בלק through עגלון.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: רות was the granddaughter of עגלון, who was the grandson of בלק king of מואב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the claim that רות came from בלק by quoting a family tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 31 only works if רות really is בלק's descendant. This statement fills in the missing link: בלק, then עגלון, then רות.

keyTerms.meaning: A king of מואב in the time of the שופטים

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
Ruth was the daughter of the son of Eglon,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל בָּלָק מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב.
phrases.english: who was the son of the son of Balak, king of Moab.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 31 that רות came from בלק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The family line given by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: בלק, then עגלון, then רות.
steps.whatToRemember: Even בלק, who brought offerings only to curse ישראל, was rewarded with רות as a descendant. That is the power of a מצוה done שלא לשמה.

steps.title: Is there reward even for refined speech?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks for the source showing that ה׳ does not hold back even the reward for speaking in a refined, modest way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא says in the name of רבי יוחנן: From where do we know that הקדוש ברוך הוא does not hold back even the reward for refined speech?
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי יוחנן asks where we learn that even a small thing like choosing modest words gets rewarded, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes back to לוט's daughters from earlier on the daf. The question sets up the claim that ה׳ rewards even small acts of refinement, and the next step will bring the proof.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba says that Rabbi Yochanan says:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַפֵּחַ
phrases.english: From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not hold back
even the reward for refined speech?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַפֵּחַ אֲפִילּוּ שְׂכַר שִׂיחָה נָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching that connects back to לוט and his daughters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that even refined speech earns reward from ה׳.

steps.title: The proof begins: how the תורה treats מואב
steps.stepSummary: The answer starts with the elder daughter, who named her son מואב. The תורה told משה only not to wage war against מואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here: as for the elder one, who called her son מואב, the Merciful One said to משה: "Do not harass מואב and do not provoke them to war." War...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן starts his proof by looking at how the תורה treats the descendants of the elder daughter. The sentence keeps going after this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elder daughter picked a name, מואב ('from father'), that openly pointed to how her son was conceived. The פסוק limits what ישראל may do to מואב mainly in the area of war, and the גמרא is about to draw an inference from that word.

phrases.english: From here:
for as for the elder one, who called him Moab,
phrases.notes: The name מואב sounds like 'from father', openly hinting at how the child was conceived.

phrases.english: the Merciful One said to Moshe:
"Do not harass Moab
and do not provoke them to war."
phrases.notes: דברים 2:9

phrases.english: War...

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵהָכָא, דְּאִילּוּ בְּכִירָה דִּקְרָיתֵיהּ מוֹאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The proof starts from the limited protection the תורה gives מואב, the son of the elder daughter, who chose an immodest name. The full contrast continues after this point.
